blocks.h2: Why Sewer Lines Fail in Lincoln Park
blocks.intro: About 1 in 3 Lincoln Park homes was built before 1940, and many of them sit on their original sewer connections.

items.body: The line from a greystone or frame house to the street sewer is often original clay, with a joint every couple of feet.
Inside the building, cast iron rusts from the inside and can split along the bottom.
On a 25-foot lot, the sewer often runs right past a parkway tree.
In a two-flat or three-flat, every unit drains into the same lateral.

blocks.h2: How We Repair a Sewer Line
blocks.intro: Once we know what's wrong, there's usually more than one way to fix it. Which method makes sense depends on the pipe's condition, location, and how it failed.
head: Method
What It Involves
Typical Disruption
rows: A resin-coated liner is pulled through the existing pipe and cured in place, creating a new pipe inside the old one.
Minimal digging, usually just small access points
A new pipe is pulled through the old one while a bursting head fractures the old pipe outward to make room.
Minimal digging, works even when the old pipe is badly damaged
The damaged section is dug up and replaced directly.
More digging, but sometimes the only option depending on damage location and access
blocks.note: Lincoln Park sewer lines often run under a front stoop, a gangway or a garden. The footage shows which method avoids tearing them up.

blocks.h2: Sewer Laterals Under Lincoln Park Greystones
blocks.body: A greystone or brick two-flat built a century ago usually sends its waste out the front, under the stoop and the parkway, to the city sewer in the street. That line may be clay, cast iron or a patchwork of both from repairs over the years. When it fails, the footage tells us where and how badly. Often the damaged section is near the foundation or under the parkway tree, and lining can fix it without opening the front walk.

blocks.h2: Sewer Repair Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: Who owns the sewer line in a Chicago two-flat?
items.preview: The building owner, in most cases.
items.answer: The building owner is responsible for the building's sewer line and for keeping it clear. In a condo building, it's usually a shared expense handled by the association.

items.q: Can a sewer repair be done without digging up the front yard?
items.answer: Often. [Trenchless lining](/chicago-lincoln-park/trenchless-sewer-repair) can rebuild the pipe from the inside through a cleanout or a small opening.

items.q: Does a repair stop backups during storms?
items.answer: A repair fixes your line, but Chicago's combined sewers can still fill up in a heavy storm. A backflow valve or [overhead sewer](/chicago-lincoln-park/overhead-sewer-systems) keeps that water out.

items.q: How old is the sewer line under my greystone?
items.preview: Possibly as old as the building.
items.answer: It could be the original line or a mix of sections replaced over the years. A [camera inspection](/chicago-lincoln-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows exactly what's there.

items.q: Will the condo association need to approve a sewer repair?
items.preview: Usually, since the line is shared.
items.answer: Usually. The lateral serves the whole building, so most associations handle it as a common expense.

items.q: How much does sewer repair cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the damage and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what the camera shows, the depth, the method and what sits above the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before any work.
